sample.from: [v for v in range(2, 31) if not is_square(v)]

params.name: m
params.resample_while: m == roots[0] or m == roots[1] or m == roots[2]

stem: Exactly one of the following numbers is undefined. Which one?
solution: A number is undefined when it contains a division by zero. A number is non-real when it has a minus sign under a square root. Check each of the four numbers for these two things.
$-\sqrt{{=n}}$ has its minus sign outside the root, not under it, and nothing is divided by zero, so it is real.
$\sqrt{-{=m}}$ has a minus sign under the square root, so it is non-real. It is not undefined, because nothing is divided by zero.
$\frac{0}{\sqrt{{=q}}}$ has the zero on top, and its denominator $\sqrt{{=q}}$ is not zero, so nothing is divided by zero. It is equal to $0$, so it is real.
$\frac{-\sqrt{{=c}}}{0}$ has $0$ in the denominator, so it has division by zero and it is undefined, whatever is on top.
notes:
Each option is a different trap from the book's own real/non-real/undefined exercise (ex1-1-3): the correct option copies the book's root-over-zero form (ex1-1-3d, ex1-11-5e); distractor 1 is the book's minus-outside-the-root case (the catalogue description says such a student calls it non-real 'or undefined'); distractor 2 is the book's negative-under-root case, picked by a student who treats non-real and undefined as one idea; distractor 3 is the book's zero-on-top case (ex1-1-3b), picked by a student who reads the zero on top as division by zero. All radicands c, n, q are non-squares chosen without repeats, and the radicand m of the non-real option is different from them, so no two options share a radicand. Exactly one option is undefined, one is non-real and two are real, for every instance. Options are expected to be shuffled by the engine.

PIPELINE NORMALISATION (not an author edit): distinct-by-choices: the stem has no {=…} hole, so it is the same sentence in every instance and only the options differ; the duplicate filter now reads stem plus options, so the family is not collapsed to one item.
